note: The outlier 201/4-03 left with no owner, measured 2026-08-30. That step recorded boot.gpuMs at 2607.5 once and 398.4 / 347.2 / 688 on later opens, and its standing hypothesis was the browser's persisted PIPELINE cache — warm on the runs it could explain, cold on the one it could not. This session produced the pair by accident and then on purpose: the panel's `webapp` job re-unpacked the served app (the assets get new identities, so the pipeline cache cannot answer for them), and the FIRST open after it cost gpuMs 5339.7 with init:pipelines 4681.1. Two further opens of the same app minutes later, nothing else changed, cost 689.2 (init:pipelines 429.1) and 404.3 (318.3). init:pipelines 4681.1 -> 429.1 is 10.9x, and it accounts for 4252 of the 4650 ms between the two boots. So the hypothesis holds and the 2607.5 outlier has an owner: a boot after an app rebuild is a COLD-pipeline boot, and it is the boot every operator takes the first time they open a new build. It is also the boot 4/03's async compile was written for, and it is still the one nobody has optimised — the 227.7 ms overlap that step bought is measured against a 690 ms warm boot, not against this. Also here, and unchanged by the cache: the world's open runs almost entirely under the GPU init - overlapMs/openMs is 99.5 % (840.5/844.3) cold and 99.4 % (619.8/623.7) warm, reproducing the 98.8 % of 2026-08-26. Device MGA-LX3 / ARM Bifrost, DPR 2. App 311f2d1. Pak: original, rect 5,-7,6,-6, textures astc, built 19:23 28-08-2026.
